skill.name: extract-design-system
skill.description: Extract design primitives from a public website and generate starter token files for a project.
skill.summary: Create starter design tokens from public website styles.
skill.author: arvindrk

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally runs external npx commands, including Playwright browser setup and the extract-design-system CLI. Most static findings are markdown backtick false positives, but the actual command instructions create normal supply-chain and untrusted-URL risks.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx commands execute packages from the public registry.
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted package versions or instruct users to review the package source before running npx commands.

remediation.issue: The extraction command accepts a user-supplied public URL.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to run extraction only against authorized public sites and avoid internal or sensitive URLs.

content.value_statement: Teams often need starter design tokens from an existing public website. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through extraction, review, and safe starter file generation.
actual_capabilities: Asks for the target public website URL before extraction.
Runs the extract-design-system CLI to collect design primitives.
Supports extraction-only mode for artifact review without starter files.
Regenerates starter token files from an existing normalized output file.
Summarizes detected colors, fonts, spacing, radii, and shadows.
Explains generated raw, normalized, JSON token, and CSS token outputs.
limitations: It extracts starter assets, not a complete component library.
It works best on public websites that are reachable and stable.
It cannot guarantee pixel-perfect reproduction of a website.
It requires confirmation before modifying existing app code or styles.

use_cases.title: Start a design token baseline
use_cases.description: Extract initial color, font, spacing, radius, and shadow values from a public brand site.

use_cases.title: Review a competitor style system
use_cases.description: Collect public visual primitives for research without claiming a complete system.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap project styling files
use_cases.description: Generate starter tokens.json and tokens.css files after reviewing normalized extraction results.

prompt_templates.title: Extract basics from a public site
prompt_templates.prompt: Use extract-design-system on this public website: <url>. Summarize the detected colors, fonts, and spacing before creating starter files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner extraction for a single public website.

prompt_templates.title: Create extraction artifacts only
prompt_templates.prompt: Run extract-design-system in extraction-only mode for <url>. Do not generate starter token files until I review the normalized output.

prompt_templates.title: Regenerate starter token files
prompt_templates.prompt: I already have .extract-design-system/normalized.json. Use extract-design-system init to regenerate starter design token files and explain the outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate files from an existing extraction artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Audit extracted primitives before adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract design primitives from <url>, then identify which values look reliable and which need manual design review before implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before adding tokens to a product codebase.

output_examples.input: Extract design primitives from a public marketing site.
output: Detected likely primary and accent colors with supporting neutral values.
Found candidate heading and body font families.
Generated starter token files after reviewing normalized results.

output_examples.input: Run extraction only and summarize the artifacts.
output: Created raw and normalized extraction artifacts for review.
Summarized colors, fonts, spacing, radius, and shadow candidates.
Did not modify existing project styles.

output_examples.input: Regenerate starter tokens from an existing normalized file.
output_examples.output: Starter token files were regenerated and explained, including their intended review workflow and adoption limits.

best_practices: Use only public websites that you are authorized to analyze.
Review normalized extraction results before adopting generated tokens.
Ask before changing existing application styles or configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one page as proof of a full product design system.
Do not overwrite an existing design system without explicit confirmation.
Do not claim extracted values are authoritative without design review.

faq.question: Does this skill build a complete component library?
faq.answer: No. It extracts starter design primitives and token files, not complete components.

faq.question: Can it analyze private websites?
faq.answer: The workflow expects a public, reachable website. Private or sensitive targets need separate authorization and setup.

faq.question: What files can it generate?
faq.answer: It can produce raw extraction data, normalized extraction data, tokens.json, and tokens.css starter files.

faq.question: Will it modify my existing app styles?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to ask for confirmation before modifying existing app code, styles, or config files.

faq.question: Why does it install Playwright Chromium?
faq.answer: The extraction workflow uses browser automation to inspect a public website and collect visual primitives.

faq.question: Should I use the generated tokens directly in production?
faq.answer: Review them first. The output is a starter point and may not represent the full website or product system.
